parsed.explanation: The parent regime governs the traveller's shared exposures: passport/visa marker restrictions, entry-screening cables inviting refusal or fraud findings on sex doubt, foreign travel advisories, federal-facility exclusion, and hostile federal custody — a tier-1/tier-2 package with inadequate remedy. The division starts there and moves up: operating anti-discrimination coverage (public accommodations, since 2008), protected facility access, a hate-crime statute with a murder conviction, changeable documents including X, courts actively ordering care resumed, and a July 2026 assessment ranking it among the most protective units. But it cannot override border, document or federal-building rules, and national funding pressure demonstrably suspends protections (youth coverage ending October 2026). No state violence data exists; custody relief came via consent decree, not a baseline rule. Score sits above the parent, below acceptance-plus-protection tiers.
